name: kuandeng/LightGCN
what_it_holds: Recommendation-systems repo that bundles a processed version of the Gowalla location check-in dataset (train.txt/test.txt user-item interaction lists plus user_list.txt/item_list.txt ID maps) alongside Yelp2018 and Amazon-book, as inputs to a graph recommender.
why_useful: CONTEXT gap #20 names Gowalla/Foursquare check-ins as party-size / cross-border tourism-flow proxies; this repo's Gowalla data is however already reduced to anonymous user-POI interaction pairs for a recommender (no raw lat/lon/timestamp), so it would need re-derivation from the original SNAP Gowalla release to recover geospatial/temporal check-in patterns — flagging as a lead, not a ready-made dataset.
geography: originally global (Gowalla was worldwide, US/EU heavy)
time_coverage: Gowalla operated 2007-2012 (service later shut down); dataset reflects that window only
size_hint: processed text files, tens of MB
license: not stated for data; code unspecified
themes: wildcard: a quant building a KPI nowcast for a consumer-internet compa
why_all: CONTEXT gap #20 names Gowalla/Foursquare check-ins as party-size / cross-border tourism-flow proxies; this repo's Gowalla data is however already reduced to anonymous user-POI interaction pairs for a recommender (no raw lat/lon/timestamp), so it would need re-derivation from the original SNAP Gowalla release to recover geospatial/temporal check-in patterns — flagging as a lead, not a ready-made dataset.

name: alexrod61/doordash-dataset
what_it_holds: Single committed CSV (`doordash.csv`), a sample of DoorDash's own historical ETA-prediction dataset (order-level features: store/market id, item counts, order value, created-at/actual-delivery timestamps), originally released by DoorDash for a takehome/Kaggle exercise. Static, one vintage, no ongoing pull.
why_useful: Order-level delivery-app data is the closest committed 'gig/platform consumer behaviour' dataset found in this sweep; could sanity-check discretionary local-spend timing patterns (order value by day-of-week/hour) as a loose cross-platform consumer-strength read, but it is a fixed historical snapshot, not a refreshable time series, so it cannot feed a quarterly forecast on its own.
time_coverage: Single historical window (exact dates not documented in README)
size_hint: One CSV, row count unspecified (parent Kaggle DoorDash ETA dataset is ~197k rows)
themes: Gig-economy and platform-economy datasets (Uber/DoorDash/Etsy/Upwork public data) used as cross-platform consumer-behaviour reads
why_all: Order-level delivery-app data is the closest committed 'gig/platform consumer behaviour' dataset found in this sweep; could sanity-check discretionary local-spend timing patterns (order value by day-of-week/hour) as a loose cross-platform consumer-strength read, but it is a fixed historical snapshot, not a refreshable time series, so it cannot feed a quarterly forecast on its own.

Real per-order delivery volume/timing data by market and date could in principle be used as a template for a food-delivery demand pace proxy (kernel analogue to booking pace), but this specific sample is a static historical ML benchmark (one company, ~2015, no recent extension), not a live or refreshable series.
